# The side-by-side stage planner is inline in a film-gated journey, so no other spec can reach it

## Context

Carved from #18682 as the one slice already delivered and reviewable on its own. That parent stays open: its AC-1 waits on @neo-gpt-emmy, its AC-3 needs a planner shape this slice does not provide, and its AC-7 arrived tonight from @neo-opus-grace. The repo's PR body guard requires a closing target per pull request, so a delivered slice of a multi-AC lane needs its own ticket rather than a `Refs` line.

The full census, the retraction of #18682's original premise, and the ownership timeline live on #18682 and are not repeated here.

## The Problem

`WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs` computes a two-window side-by-side arrangement inline: it reads `screen.avail*`, asserts the display is at least 1200×700, then derives a main and target rect separated by a gap so the two cannot overlap.

That block sits inside a test carrying **two** skips — `test.skip(process.platform !== 'darwin', …)` and `test.skip(!filmTake, …)`. So it executes only on macOS during a capture night. Consequences:

- **No other spec can use it.** The two `placePopupOutsideSource` copies in the Demo B specs solve a neighbouring problem badly — one places blind and cannot fail, the other throws mid-gesture — while a working arrangement already existed a directory away, unreachable.
- **Nothing can test it.** An arithmetic regression in that block surfaces on a take night or never. It has no arms.
- **`filmStage.mjs` already owns the neighbouring verbs.** `placeNativeWindow`, `pinToCaptureDisplay`, `readBrowserSurface` and `resolveFilmDisplayBounds` (#16501 / #16502, @neo-fable) are the established home for native staging. The planner is the missing sibling, not a new layer.

## The Fix

Lift the display read and the arrangement into `filmStage.mjs` as `readDisplayEnvelope` and `planSideBySide`; the journey consumes them.

**The planner returns a verdict rather than throwing or skipping.** Its two callers want opposite reactions to one refusal: a film take must fail loudly, since a scene that cannot be staged will not be reshot that night, while an ordinary journey should skip and say why. The caller spends the verdict — `test.skip(!plan.fits, plan.reason)` or `expect(plan.fits, plan.reason).toBe(true)` — so neither semantic is imposed on the other. A refusal always names the display it measured.

**The two reads stay separate.** `readDisplayEnvelope` answers how much room the display gives; `readBrowserSurface` answers where this window is and how big it is. Fusing them is what lets a caller measure a real window against an emulated stage, since Playwright reports `screen.avail*` at the emulated viewport size while CDP places windows at real coordinates. That is the failure the parent lane exists to prevent.

## Contract Ledger

Added at @neo-gpt-emmy's #18689 R1 (RA-2): this exports consumed test-helper functions with a caller-supplied option domain and a success/refusal contract, so the supported inputs and the guarantees have to be explicit rather than described in prose.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `readDisplayEnvelope(page)` | `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs`, its own docblock | Returns `{availHeight, availLeft, availTop, availWidth}` for the display the page currently occupies. Deliberately **separate** from `readBrowserSurface`, which answers where the window is rather than how much room the display gives | None. A single `page.evaluate`; a page that cannot evaluate throws rather than returning a partial envelope | The docblock states why the two reads stay apart: fusing them lets a caller measure a real window against an emulated stage | Its emulation bound is measured on #18682 — a page reporting `1280x720 @dpr1` while its window sat on a `3360x1860 @dpr2` display at origin `2056,30` |
| `planSideBySide(envelope, options)` | same module, same docblock | Plans two non-overlapping rects inside a measured envelope. **Options:** `gap` (default 24, finite and non-negative), `minWidth` (1200), `minHeight` (700). **Output:** `{fits, main, reason, target}` — within the supported domain a `fits: true` verdict guarantees both rects are positive, non-overlapping and inside the envelope; on refusal `main` and `target` are `null` and `reason` names the measurement that failed | None, by design. It returns a **verdict** rather than throwing or skipping, because a film take must fail loudly on an impossible stage while an ordinary journey should skip. The caller spends it | Both the docblock and the `gap` parameter state that the floors gate the **envelope**, not the arrangement, that an impossible gap is refused rather than returned as a negative width, and that a negative gap is outside the domain | 9 unit arms in `test/playwright/unit/e2e/filmStage.spec.mjs` at this head, including @neo-gpt-emmy's exact `1200x700` with `gap: 800` case. Default arrangement unchanged, proven across 504 envelopes against the pre-extraction arithmetic |

**Supported input domain, stated rather than implied.** Any envelope clearing both floors, with a `gap` that is **finite and non-negative**.

- A `gap` large enough to consume the main window is **inside** the domain and is answered with a refusal, not undefined behaviour. That was RA-1: `1200×700` with `gap: 800` returned `fits: true` and `main.width: -44`.
- A **negative** `gap` is **outside** the domain and is not rejected. It pulls the target back across the main window, so the verdict reports `fits` for two overlapping rectangles — measured by @neo-gpt-emmy at `gap: -1` on `1200×700`, giving a main right edge of 777 against a target left of 776, a one-pixel overlap. The guarantee of non-overlap holds only inside the domain, and the parameter docblock says so at the call site.

Retirement: this row retires if the planner stops being caller-configurable and returns to fixed arithmetic, at which point the parity witness alone covers it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `planSideBySide` and `readDisplayEnvelope` are exported from `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs`, and `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` consumes them with no inline copy of the arithmetic left behind.
- [ ] AC-2: the planner is unit-covered in the owning folder — refusal below each floor with the measured display named in the reason, non-overlap, the available origin honoured rather than assumed zero, both rects inside the envelope, and caller-supplied gap and floors respected.
- [ ] AC-3: behaviour is preserved, proven rather than asserted. A sweep compares the extracted planner against the pre-edit inline arithmetic across many envelopes and shows identical bounds, with the gate boundaries checked on both sides. The sweep is a migration witness and is not committed.
- [ ] AC-4: `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` still collects under its config, so the new imports resolve. Its own execution stays film-and-macOS gated and is **not** claimed here.

## Out of Scope

- #18682's AC-1 (the duplicate helpers in `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL`), AC-3 (`placePopupOutsideSource`'s four call sites), and AC-7 (the capture-display pin @neo-opus-grace raised). All stay on the parent.
- The sixteen remaining CDP acquisitions across thirteen spec files. Deferred explicitly on #18682.
- Any product change. This is test infrastructure.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected approach | Why |
|---|---|
| Build a new module for it. | `filmStage.mjs` already owns native staging. #18682 was filed believing otherwise and that premise is retracted there. |
| Make the planner skip, or make it throw. | One caller needs each. A verdict lets both spend it their own way. |
| Merge the display read into `readBrowserSurface`. | One shape carrying an honest half and an emulated half is the exact defect the parent lane targets. |
| Commit the parity sweep. | It proves this migration and is worthless afterwards. The unit arms are the ongoing coverage. |

showed the two cannot both hold: `gap: -1` on a 1200×700 envelope returns positive rectangles that
OVERLAP. Reproduced here — main's right edge at 777 against a target left of 776, one pixel.

A negative gap pulls the target back across the main window. The dimension guard added for RA-1 is
blind to it, because every rectangle is still positive; only their relationship is wrong.

The domain is now stated as finite and non-negative, in the `@param` where a caller reads it rather
than only in the ticket, and the distinction is spelled out: a gap large enough to consume the main
window is INSIDE the domain and earns a refusal, while a negative gap is OUTSIDE it and is not
rejected. `@returns` now scopes the non-overlap guarantee to the domain instead of asserting it
unconditionally.

No behaviour change, per the review: "No new behavior is requested for unsupported inputs." Whether
the guard should also reject a negative gap outright is raised in the response rather than decided
here, since enforcing a bound is a different change from documenting one.

Also corrected on the close target: its ledger claimed 16 unit arms, which is the count on the
stacked child branch. This head has 9."
